title: Config Sherpa: state reconciler & cost-aware trigger heuristics for safe undo
creator: Priya Kulkarni
description:
Problem: configuration changes to autoscaling, batching, and KV cache policies have previously caused subtle regressions that increase per-token cost or latency without immediate obvious failures. We need an automated rollback system that can detect harmful config changes early, reconcile divergent node state, and apply safe undo steps while minimizing customer impact and cost churn.

Scope: build 'Config Sherpa' — a small orchestration service and set of heuristics that watch config-change events, compute cost/latency deltas from telemetry, and decide whether to auto-revert, trigger a gated rollback, or escalate to humans. The system must include:
- Cost-aware triggers (thresholds and rate of change heuristics using 1m/5m/15m windows)
- Guardrails for noisy signals (hysteresis, backoff, synthetic canary replay)
- State reconciliation (ensure KV cache and batching settings across serving nodes converge; detect partial-apply drift)
- Safe apply plan (staged rollouts, shadow apply, preflight simulated load when possible)
- Clear audit trail and runbook links for on-call to follow up.

Non-goals: full feature toggle management UI (console work will be follow-up), cross-region traffic shaping (separate project).
acceptance_criteria: New Config Sherpa service subscribed to config-change stream and logs decision events to telemetry
At least three cost-aware trigger heuristics implemented (absolute per-token increase, gradient over 5m, spike detection) with configurable thresholds
A reconciliation run can detect partial-applies across >90% of nodes and surface corrective actions (resync or staged revert)
Automated safety flow will run a lightweight synthetic canary for changes to batching/prefix cache when enabled
Audit events with reason and selected fallback are written to the Config Change history and incident log
E2E test harness simulating a bad batching config demonstrates an automatic gated rollback path in CI
success_metrics: Reduce mean time to detect cost regressions from config changes from 3 hours to <30 minutes
Reduce number of manual rollbacks by 50% in the first quarter after rollout
False positive auto-revert rate <5% on historical canary dataset
Telemetry shows no >15% sustained latency increase during automated recovery windows

updates: 2026-02-25 - Decision: Use a combined signal of per-token cost delta and latency gradient rather than single-signal threshold to reduce noisy reverts.

2026-03-02 - Trade-off: To avoid cascading rollbacks, initial rollout will only attempt automated revert for non-security changes and when confidence >= 0.7. Lower confidence triggers human notification.
2026-03-06 - Implementation note: Reconciliation will operate in two phases: detection (stateless scan) and corrective action (transactional batched apply with pre/post snapshots).
2026-03-10 - Review feedback from Platform leads: add explicit 'quarantine' mode that isolates suspect nodes from serving traffic while allowing fast resync tests.
2026-03-12 - QA: E2E synthetic test added to CI that simulates a bad batching configuration; observed automated gated rollback path works in staging (PRs referenced).
